# ASTRA

> ASTRA (Agentic Schema for Transparent Research Analysis) records a research analysis: the files it reads, the outputs it makes, the decisions it makes along the way, the universes it makes them in, and the claims it rests on them. An analysis is a folder with an `astra.yaml` at its top, in a git repository. This file is a short briefing for AI agents that write or read ASTRA analyses; the specification is the authority.

## The analysis document

An `astra.yaml` is a YAML 1.2 document whose content is a map. Every element the author names is an entry of a map keyed by its id, written once as the key: a lowercase letter `a`-`z`, then any number of lowercase letters, digits and `_`.

- `spec_version` (required): the version of the specification the file is written against, a string such as `"0.1.0"`.
- `inputs`: the files the analysis reads. Each has a `path`, relative to the folder of the `astra.yaml`, to one file tracked in git with the analysis. Data not tracked in git with the analysis comes in through an output whose recipe gets it.
- `decisions`: the choices the analysis makes, each with its `rationale` and at least one of its `options`. An option can list options it `requires` or is `incompatible_with` (as `decision.option`), cite the prior `insights` that support it, or be `excluded` with a reason: it stays listed, and no universe selects it.
- `outputs`: what the analysis makes. Each has a `type` (`metric`, `figure`, `table`, `data` or `report`), a `format` (the file extension, without the dot, such as `csv`), the `inputs` it is made from (inputs, outputs and switches, in order), the `decisions` it is made with directly, and a `recipe`, unless it is a switch.
- `recipe`: a `command`, a POSIX shell command run in the analysis's folder, optionally with `resources`. A runner fills in its placeholders verbatim, with no shell quoting: `{inputs.<entry>}` and `{inputs}` (paths), `{decisions.<entry>}` (the selected option's id) and `{output}` (the path to write). Each `<entry>` is an entry of the output's `inputs` or `decisions`, exactly as written; `{{` and `}}` are literal braces.
- A switch is an entry of `outputs` with a `switch`, a decision's address, and `cases` from that decision's options to references, such as `switch: decision1` with `cases: {a: output1, b: stage.output3}`; it has no `type`, `format`, `inputs`, `decisions` or `recipe`. In each universe it is read as the case of the option selected there, so `{inputs.<entry>}` of an output reading it is that case's path. Where the option has no case, the switch isn't built, nor is anything that reads it without a pin. For two decisions, nest switches, the one that decides whether the other matters outside.
- `universes`: each selects one option for each decision it uses, as `decisions: {decision1: a}`; a decision that only an unbuilt branch uses need not be set, and a universe's own `decisions` set no decision that none of its branches uses. With `derived_from`, a universe inherits another's selection and gives only what it changes. No universe is privileged: there is no default universe or option. An entry can instead import a universe of a declared analysis, with `analysis` and `universe`.
- `prior_insights` (what earlier work establishes) and `findings` (what the analysis concludes): each has a `claim` and at least one item of `evidence`, which cites exactly one of a published work, by `doi`, and an output, as `artifact`. Evidence can quote the passage (`quote`, with `exact`) and locate it (`location`, with a fragment identifier such as `page=6`).
- `analyses`: the other analyses this one declares, each by `path`, or by `url` and `commit`. Their elements are named by address, `<declaration>.<element>`, such as `subanalysis.output1`.

Most elements also take a `label`, a `description` and `tags`. Every field is in the field reference.

## A minimal analysis

```yaml
spec_version: "0.1.0"
label: Example analysis

inputs:
  input1:
    path: data/input1.csv

decisions:
  decision1:
    rationale: Both are reasonable, and they may give different results.
    options:
      a: {}
      b: {}

outputs:
  output1:
    type: metric
    format: json
    inputs: [input1]
    decisions: [decision1]
    recipe:
      command: >-
        python src/output1.py '{inputs.input1}' '{decisions.decision1}'
        '{output}'
  output2:
    type: table
    format: csv
    inputs: [output1#u1, output1#u2]
    recipe:
      command: >-
        python src/output2.py '{inputs.output1#u1}' '{inputs.output1#u2}'
        '{output}'

universes:
  u1:
    decisions: {decision1: a}
  u2:
    decisions: {decision1: b}

findings:
  insight1:
    claim: Options a and b of decision1 give different results.
    evidence:
      - artifact: output2
```

`output1` lists `decision1`, so it is built per universe, once in `u1` and once in `u2`. `output2` reads it pinned to each universe, `output1#u1` and `output1#u2`, so it is built once, from both.

## Building and checking

- An output is built per universe when it lists `decisions` or reads, without a pin, a switch or an output built per universe. Any other output is built once. A switch has no result: reading it reads the case it takes.
- The analysis plans its own outputs and switches that nothing of its own reads; an output that only a switch's case names is planned only where that case is taken, unless something else reads it or a finding cites it.
- A pin, `#` and a universe's id, reads an output as built in that universe, so one output can compare universes.
- A declared analysis's decisions can be set from this analysis's universes, under keys such as `subanalysis.decision1`: its universes then drive it.
- A runner writes each result's bytes at `results/{universe}/{name}.{format}` (or `results/{name}.{format}` when built once) and a JSON record of the run that made it under `.astra/records/`, in the folder of the analysis the result belongs to.
- A recipe should read the files inputs name, and other outputs' results, only through its output's `inputs`: a checker sees a change to them only there.
- A checker gives each planned result a record status, `unchanged`, `stale` or `missing`, and a bytes status, `present` or `absent`.

## Docs

- [Specification](https://astra-spec.org/latest/specification/): how ASTRA works, and every rule, each with its code.
- [Rules](https://astra-spec.org/latest/specification/#rules): every rule, by layer, each with its code.
- [Field reference](https://astra-spec.org/latest/elements/): every field of `astra.yaml` and of a record.

## Examples

- [iris](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LightconeResearch/astra-spec/main/examples/iris/astra.yaml): one analysis with decisions, constraints between options, two universes, and an output built once that compares them through pins.
- [iris_pipeline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LightconeResearch/astra-spec/main/examples/iris_pipeline/astra.yaml): a root analysis that declares two stages, `feature_extraction` and `classification`, and drives their decisions from its universes.
